instructions.content: Apply JSON Canvas when creating/editing .canvas files, mind maps, or flowcharts; do not apply it for a Markdown note, a database view, or a diagram meant to render to image/PDF.
instructions.original_snippets: When to apply: Creating or editing .canvas files ... When NOT to apply: The user wants a Markdown note, a database view (use Bases), or a diagram format that outputs to image/PDF

instructions.content: A canvas file's two top-level arrays are nodes and edges; both are optional but the file must contain this base structure.
instructions.original_snippets: A canvas file (.canvas) contains two top-level arrays ... {"nodes": [], "edges": []}

instructions.content: Generate a unique 16-character lowercase hexadecimal ID for every node and edge.
instructions.original_snippets: Generate unique 16-character hex IDs for each node (e.g., "6f0ad84f44ce9c17")

instructions.content: When adding a node, choose a position that does not overlap existing nodes, leaving 50-100px spacing.
instructions.original_snippets: Choose position (x, y) that avoids overlapping existing nodes (leave 50-100px spacing)

instructions.content: After creating or editing a canvas, validate that all IDs are unique and every fromNode/toNode reference resolves to an existing node ID.
instructions.original_snippets: Validate: Confirm all IDs are unique and all edge references resolve to existing nodes

instructions.content: Array order of nodes determines z-index: the first node is the bottom layer and the last is the top layer.
instructions.original_snippets: Nodes are objects placed on the canvas. Array order determines z-index: first node = bottom layer, last node = top layer.

instructions.content: Each node type has an extra required field: text nodes need text, file nodes need file, link nodes need url, group nodes need none.
instructions.original_snippets: text | text (string) | Markdown content ... file | file (path) ... link | url (string) ... group | none

instructions.content: NEVER embed a literal newline in a JSON string value; use the \n escape instead.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER embed literal newlines in JSON string values -- use \n.

instructions.content: NEVER use a literal double-backslash-n (\\n); it renders as a literal backslash-n on screen instead of a line break.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use \\n -- it renders as literal backslash-n on screen.

instructions.content: NEVER reuse the same id across nodes or edges; duplicates silently overwrite each other with no error.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER reuse the same id across nodes or edges -- duplicates silently overwrite each other with no error.

instructions.content: NEVER reference a fromNode/toNode ID that does not exist in nodes; the edge renders invisibly with no error.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER reference a fromNode/toNode ID that does not exist in nodes -- the edge renders invisibly.

instructions.content: NEVER place child nodes outside the group's coordinate bounds; they appear as free-floating items instead of being contained.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER place child nodes outside the group's coordinate bounds -- they appear as free-floating items.

instructions.content: NEVER set fromEnd/toEnd to anything other than none or arrow; other values are silently discarded.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER set fromEnd/toEnd to anything other than "none" or "arrow" -- other values are silently discarded.

instructions.content: NEVER supply a bare integer for color; the canvasColor type requires a quoted string such as "1", not 1.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER supply a bare integer for color -- the canvasColor type requires a quoted string ("1", not 1).

instructions.content: Run the full validation checklist after any edit: unique IDs, resolvable edge references, required fields present per node type, enumerated field values valid, and the JSON itself parseable.
instructions.original_snippets: After creating or editing a canvas file, verify: 1. All id values are unique ... 8. JSON is valid and parseable
